favourite.heading: Why Western Michigan can pull away
bullets: Western Michigan is the better football team by 15.6 points on opponent-adjusted results — but about 86% of that rating is still last season carried forward, and in a portal era last season is a different team (-15.6 pts).
Stylistically the matchup favours Western Michigan by 0.4 points: early-down offence vs early-down defence (-0.4 pts).

underdog.heading: Why Rice can keep it close
bullets: Conference strength differs and the in-season sample is still thin, worth 5.7 points to Rice (+5.7 pts).
Playing at Rice is worth 4.1 points — the league-wide home-field number, because a per-venue table was tested and could not be told apart from the home team’s own quality (+4.1 pts).
The outcome range is 15.5 points wide at one sigma — p10 -30.2 to p90 +14.8 for Rice, so a projection of -6.2 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 6%.
60% of the model’s own input contract was empty for this game — no starter, injury or per-player talent context reached it, so the number leans on team strength more than it should.
